h: Rose Street rules of the game
p: Getting here couldn't be simpler. Edinburgh Waverley station is a few minutes' walk away, just down at the eastern end of Princes Street, and the trams run along Princes Street too, linking the city centre to the airport. If you're staying in the Old Town, it's a short walk across the valley via the Mound or one of the bridges.

A couple of tips for your visit. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues in Scotland commonly check, and it saves any disappointment at the door. Book a lane ahead, especially in August when the festivals bring huge crowds into the city, and think about two lanes if you're a big group. Swapping teams halfway through keeps the banter flowing.

If you've got time before or after a game, there's a lot within a few minutes' walk. The Scott Monument, the towering Gothic spire on Princes Street, is a famous landmark you can climb for views over the city. The Scottish National Gallery sits at the foot of the Mound, and St Andrew Square, at the eastern end of George Street, is a pleasant green spot for a sit-down.

Fancy a bit of fresh air? Calton Hill, a short walk east, gives you one of the best views in the city, with its monuments and panoramas across to Arthur's Seat and the Firth of Forth. Perfect for working up an appetite before your game.
